chunks: To your Lord then will be the driving.
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'To your Lord then will be the driving' mean in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Fajr (89:25) underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah, contrasting the transient power of worldly tyrants with the ultimate authority of the Creator. It serves as a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, all creation will be driven back to their Lord for reckoning, affirming the inevitability of divine justice and the final return to God.
